QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_47

question.text: Under SAS-500, if the SE's environmental-programme area overlaps with a state-funded MGNREGA watershed, attribution becomes complex. The DEFENSIBLE approach is:

answer.text: Allocate impact between SE and MGNREGA based on relative expenditure, activities and timing — disclose the allocation assumption explicitly in the Report
Combine into a single number without disclosure

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Co-funding allocation needs an explicit rule (expenditure-based, activity-based, or time-based) and disclosure of the rule. The user of the Report must see the basis of attribution. Concealing overlap violates SAS-500 transparency. **The Trap:** Option B overclaims. Option C ignores the confounder. Option D hides the assumption. **Cross-Exam Context:** Same allocation-rule-disclosure in X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser — shared advice) and III-A / III-C Compliance. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Build a simple attribution matrix: Column 1 = activity; Column 2 = SE spend %; Column 3 = Govt-scheme spend %; Column 4 = attributed outcome %. One page, one disclosure.
